newsitem.title: JAPAN: Croatia may seek credit rating from Japan firms.
newsitem.headline: Croatia may seek credit rating from Japan firms.

text.p: Croatia hopes to receive credit ratings from Japanese rating agencies at some time in the future, a Japanese banker quoted Croatian officials as telling an investment seminar on Tuesday.
They also reiterated their interest in raising funds in the longer term by issuing yen-based bonds, he said.
The seminar, held to drum up interest in Croatia's debut Eurobond issue, was closed to the press and limited to a small number of investors, as the planned issue will be privately placed.
"Croatia expressed its interest in receiving credit ratings from Japanese agencies for the purpose of raising funds in yen by issuing bonds in the long-term future," the seminar participant said.

On Monday, Croatian Finance Minister Bozo Prka told Reuters in an interview that Croatia would start with U.S. dollar and German mark denominated Eurobonds, but may issue bonds in the Japanese samurai and U.S. yankee bond markets in the future.

Croatia plans to launch a $250 million five-year Eurobond following a whirlwind global roadshow that began on Monday in Hong Kong and will travel from Asia to the United States and Europe. The final presentation will be in London on February 5.
The minister estimated Croatia's gross borrowing requirements for 1997 at $1 billion.
"Detailed terms of the Eurobond issue were not mentioned at the seminar," the banker said. "But considering the size and maturity (of the bonds), I expect they will be well-absorbed."
On Friday, Standard & Poor's and IBCA both assigned a BBB minus long-term foreign currency rating to Croatia and S&P said it had assigned its A minus long-term local currency rating.
An official of a major Japanese rating agency, Japan Bond Research Institute (JBRI), said JBRI had not yet been contacted by the Croatian government.

"We have not taken a close look at Croatia. There may be a negative image about the country because of the war," the JBRI official said. "But in terms of the economy, Croatia seems to be performing well."
